question: Why were so many Victorian novels, from Dickens onwards, built to end each monthly part on a hook?
answer: Because readers paid by the instalment. Dickens's publishers sold The Pickwick Papers in monthly parts at a shilling each, so families who could not afford a whole novel could follow one; by the end tens of thousands bought each part. Every part had to bring buyers back. The price shaped the plot.
move: How people pay for something shapes what gets made for them.
ask: How does the way I am paid shape the work I actually do?
source: Patten, Charles Dickens and His Publishers, 1978
reference: Robert L. Patten, Charles Dickens and His Publishers, Clarendon Press, 1978
